sources.entry: black - The uncompromising Python code formatter.

summary.one_liner: Black is an opinionated, uncompromising Python code formatter that rewrites files in place to a single consistent PEP 8-compliant style.
summary.what_it_does: Black reformats entire Python files in place according to its own fixed code style, with very few configuration options. It aims for deterministic output and the smallest possible diffs, so code review focuses on content rather than formatting. Before writing changes, it checks that the reformatted code still produces a valid AST effectively equivalent to the original; the --fast flag skips this check. It can read project-specific defaults for its command-line options from a pyproject.toml file, including include and exclude patterns. Black can also format Jupyter Notebooks when installed with the jupyter extra. The README also points to separate documents covering the current and future style, a stability policy, and a "pragmatism" document describing exceptions to its rules.
use_cases: Auto-format Python source files consistently across a project
Reduce formatting noise in code reviews
Enforce a shared Python code style in continuous integration
Configure include and exclude patterns for formatting via pyproject.toml
notable: Deliberately limited configuration options; aims for sensible defaults out of the box
Checks that reformatted code is AST-equivalent to the original unless --fast is used
Published style documentation with separate current style, future style, and stability policy
Available as standalone PyInstaller executables without a Python install
Widely adopted by large projects such as pytest, Django, and pandas, according to the README
caveats: Style is intentionally opinionated, so little customization is available
AST safety check slows processing unless --fast is used
